project.name: Routr
project.title: How much SIP traffic Routr handles.
project.lead: We run these tests after significant changes to the code, on dedicated DigitalOcean servers, one for Routr and one for the load generator. The EdgePort runs alone to find its limit; the whole stack runs for hours to catch leaks.

narrative.what: The EdgePort on its own, with Echo answering every request with 200 OK. No Dispatcher, Connect or database, so this is a ceiling for EdgePort alone, not for a full deployment.
narrative.why: The EdgePort is the only stateful piece of Routr. When it saturates, calls fail, no matter what runs behind it.
narrative.how: Smoke run: SIPp sends SIP MESSAGE requests over UDP, starting at 25 messages/s and adding 25 every minute, up to 200 messages/s. The first 30 s warm the EdgePort up and are not measured. The run stops at the first step where p99 MESSAGE-to-200 latency reaches 50 ms or failed requests reach 0.1%.

narrative.what: The whole stack in one image, EdgePort plus Dispatcher, Connect, Location and the data service in one Node process, routing calls between registered agents.
narrative.why: Leaks only show after hours. A short test can pass while memory climbs until the process is killed in production.
narrative.how: Smoke run: SIPp holds a steady 1 call/s for 3 minutes, with 200 registered callee agents, each called by its own caller agent through Connect. After a 1-minute warm-up, each process's memory may grow at most 5 MB/h.
